plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A classic autumn perennial with dense, layered blooms in a huge range of forms, from daisy-like to pompon and spider types. It thrives in cool fall weather and is often the last garden flower to bloom before hard frost.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide; native to East Asia (China and Japan); widely grown in temperate gardens of North America and Europe
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are the national flower of Japan, and the Imperial Seal of Japan is a stylized 16-petaled chrysanthemum. Blooming is triggered by shortening day length.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub that blooms in late autumn, earlier than the more familiar Camellia japonica. It has glossy dark green leaves and fragrant, delicate single or semi-double flowers with prominent yellow stamens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter (October to December)
plants.location: Native to southern Japan; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Mediterranean Europe, and mild-climate gardens
plants.funFact: Sasanqua camellias are related to the tea plant (Camellia sinensis), and oil pressed from their seeds is used in Japan for cooking and hair care.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spectacular tropical to subtropical tree that covers itself in clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In bloom the canopy appears as a purple cloud, and fallen petals carpet streets and lawns.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November)
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); famously planted in Pretoria and Johannesburg in South Africa, Brisbane and Sydney in Australia, and Buenos Aires
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, which is nicknamed the Jacaranda City, there are tens of thousands of these trees, and an old student superstition says that a blossom falling on your head brings good luck in exams.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A bold evergreen shrub that produces the largest flower heads in the protea family, with a bowl of pointed bracts surrounding a central cone of tiny true flowers. It thrives in the nutrient-poor, fire-prone fynbos habitat.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (August to November, peaking in spring)
plants.location: Native to the Western and Eastern Cape of South Africa; cultivated in California, Hawaii, Australia, and Portugal
plants.funFact: The king protea is the national flower of South Africa, and its genus is named after Proteus, the Greek sea god who could change shape, a nod to the plant family's great diversity.
